explicacion.en: English “unless” is a single word, so learners drop que. The fixed phrase is a menos que, always with que.

titulo.en: Unless: a menos que + subjunctive

texto.en: A menos que means “unless”. Spanish always puts the verb after it in the subjunctive, because the condition is only a possibility and it is not a fact yet. English says “unless it includes” with a normal present tense, so English speakers often write incluye. In Spanish it must be incluya: No firmo a menos que incluya el seguro. Use the present subjunctive when the condition is about the present or the future: Salimos a las seis, a menos que llueva. The main verb can be affirmative or negative. A menos que already contains the idea of “if not”, so do not add another no: it is a menos que incluya, not a menos que no incluya. Also keep que: English has one word, “unless”, but Spanish needs the full phrase a menos que. It is similar to salvo que and excepto si.

titulo.en: A hypothesis: a menos que + imperfect subjunctive

texto.en: You already know the imperfect subjunctive (quería que me hablaran) and the conditional (haría). When the situation is only imaginary, the main verb goes in the conditional and the verb after a menos que goes in the imperfect subjunctive: No lo haría a menos que me pagaran más. Do not use the imperfect indicative (pagaban) here, even though English says “unless they paid me”. Compare it with con tal de que, which you have already studied: it also takes the subjunctive, but it names a condition that you want to be fulfilled. Firmo con tal de que incluya el seguro = I sign as long as it includes the insurance. A menos que names the exception: No firmo a menos que incluya el seguro = I don't sign, except if it includes it. With a real, simple condition you can also use si and the indicative: Si incluye el seguro, firmo.

contexto.en: A February morning in 2031, at a vehicle rental agency in Quito. Emma, who coordinates projects at Andes Vivos, needs a van to take a group to Mindo. She talks to the Empleada, and they address each other as usted. Emma has not signed yet: she wants to read the fine print and will come back on the day of the trip.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días. Necesito alquilar una van para ocho pasajeros durante tres días. Trabajo en Andes Vivos, una fundación de turismo comunitario, y vamos a llevar a un grupo de turistas a Mindo.

traduccion.en: Good morning. I need to rent a van for eight passengers for three days. I work at Andes Vivos, a community tourism foundation, and we are going to take a group of tourists to Mindo.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, señora. Sí, tenemos una van de ocho pasajeros para esas fechas. Al recoger la van, se paga un depósito de quinientos dólares.

traduccion.en: Good morning, ma'am. Yes, we have an eight-passenger van for those dates. When you pick up the van, a deposit of five hundred dollars is paid.

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. Pero le aviso algo desde ahora: no firmo a menos que el contrato incluya el seguro completo.

traduccion.en: I understand. But I'll tell you something right now: I won't sign unless the contract includes full insurance.

traduccion.en: Don't worry, the full insurance is already included in the rate.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. ¿Hay algún recargo? Quiero saber el precio final antes de decidir.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Is there any surcharge? I want to know the final price before deciding.

traduccion.en: There are no surcharges, unless the van is returned with an empty tank. In that case the fuel and a service surcharge are charged.

traduccion.en: That's fine. We are going to return the van with a full tank. Now I want to read the fine print, if that's not a problem.

dialogo.texto: Claro que sí. Aquí tiene el contrato.

traduccion.en: Of course. Here is the contract.

dialogo.texto: Gracias. Aquí hay una estipulación sobre las carreteras. ¿Puedo llevar la van a Mindo?

traduccion.en: Thank you. Here there is a stipulation about roads. Can I take the van to Mindo?

dialogo.texto: Sí, no hay problema. La estipulación más importante es que la van no puede salir del país.

traduccion.en: Yes, no problem. The most important stipulation is that the van cannot leave the country.

dialogo.texto: Entendido. Y aquí hay una franquicia. ¿Qué significa?

traduccion.en: Understood. And here there is a deductible. What does it mean?

traduccion.en: It is the part of the damage that the customer pays. If there is a scratch or a dent, you pay one hundred dollars and the insurance pays the rest.

traduccion.en: No, the fuel is not included. The van leaves with a full tank and you return it with a full tank.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Then I'll write him down as the additional driver. One more thing: if you cancel less than two days in advance, there is a penalty.

explicacion.en: English “in the event that” has no little word like de, so learners drop it. The fixed phrase is en el supuesto de que.

titulo.en: In the event that: en el supuesto de que + subjunctive

texto.en: En el supuesto de que is a formal way to pose a scenario: it means “in the event that” or “assuming that”. The verb that follows is always in the present subjunctive, because the scenario has not happened and may never happen: En el supuesto de que haya un retraso, el banco avisará. Keep the de: the whole phrase is en el supuesto de que, and English speakers who say “in the event that” often drop it. It belongs to the same family as en caso de que, which you already know, and it is also close to suponiendo que and siempre y cuando. You hear it in banks, insurance offices and contracts. The sentence usually has two parts: the scenario and its consequence.

titulo.en: The consequence, and asking for guarantees

texto.en: The main clause says what will happen. It can be in the future (el banco avisará), in the present (la póliza cubre los daños) or an imperative (llame al banco): En el supuesto de que pierda la tarjeta, llame al banco. The scenario can come first or last: El banco cobrará un interés de mora en el supuesto de que haya un retraso. This phrase is also a polite way to ask for guarantees: ¿Qué pasa en el supuesto de que no podamos pagar una cuota? Compare it with a menos que: En el supuesto de que haya un retraso only poses a scenario and then says its consequence, while a menos que names an exception: No hay interés, a menos que el retraso supere treinta días. Both take the subjunctive. With the main verb in the present or future, use the present subjunctive.

contexto.en: A February morning in 2031, a few days after the visit to the rental agency. At a bank branch in Quito, Emma applies for a small loan to buy equipment for a community that works with Andes Vivos. She talks to the Ejecutiva, and they address each other as usted. Emma wants to know what happens in different scenarios before she signs.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, señora García. ¿En qué le puedo ayudar?

traduccion.en: Good morning, Ms. García. How can I help you?

dialogo.texto: Buenos días. Trabajo en Andes Vivos y quiero solicitar un préstamo pequeño para comprar equipos para una comunidad con la que trabajamos.

traduccion.en: Good morning. I work at Andes Vivos and I want to apply for a small loan to buy equipment for a community we work with.

dialogo.texto: Con mucho gusto. Para un préstamo pequeño, el trámite es sencillo. ¿Qué preguntas tiene?

traduccion.en: With pleasure. For a small loan, the procedure is simple. What questions do you have?

dialogo.texto: Antes de firmar, quiero entender los riesgos. ¿Qué pasa en el supuesto de que la comunidad se retrase con una cuota?

traduccion.en: Before signing, I want to understand the risks. What happens in the event that the community is late with an installment?

dialogo.texto: Las cuotas se pagan hasta la fecha de corte de cada mes. En el supuesto de que el retraso supere los treinta días, el banco cobrará un interés de mora.

traduccion.en: The installments are paid by the cut-off date each month. In the event that the delay exceeds thirty days, the bank will charge late-payment interest.

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. ¿Y si queremos cancelar el préstamo antes de terminar?

traduccion.en: I understand. And what if we want to cancel the loan before it ends?

dialogo.texto: Es posible. En el supuesto de que el préstamo se cancele antes, no hay penalización.

traduccion.en: That's possible. In the event that the loan is cancelled early, there is no penalty.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. ¿Cuándo hace el banco el desembolso?

traduccion.en: Perfect. When does the bank make the disbursement?

traduccion.en: The disbursement is made two days after signing the contract.

dialogo.texto: Los equipos van a ser nuevos. ¿El banco ofrece algún seguro?

traduccion.en: The equipment is going to be new. Does the bank offer any insurance?

dialogo.texto: Sí, hay un seguro para los equipos. La prima es pequeña y se paga una vez al año. El asegurado sería Andes Vivos.

traduccion.en: Yes, there is an insurance for the equipment. The premium is small and is paid once a year. The insured party would be Andes Vivos.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y qué incluye la cobertura?

traduccion.en: And what does the coverage include?

dialogo.texto: Incluye el robo y los incendios. En el supuesto de que haya un siniestro, la póliza cubre los daños.

traduccion.en: It includes theft and fires. In the event of an insured accident, the policy covers the damage.

dialogo.texto: ¿Cuánto tiempo tiene la comunidad para pagar el préstamo?

traduccion.en: How much time does the community have to pay the loan?

dialogo.texto: Doce meses, con una cuota cada mes: son doce cuotas. Necesito su cédula, el aval y una carta de la comunidad que explique para qué son los equipos.

traduccion.en: Twelve months, with one installment each month: that is twelve installments. I need your ID card, the guarantee and a letter from the community explaining what the equipment is for.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. ¿Qué garantía necesita el banco?

traduccion.en: Very good. What guarantee does the bank need?

dialogo.texto: Como garantía, el banco necesita el aval de Andes Vivos, firmado por la directora, Inés Cárdenas.

traduccion.en: As a guarantee, the bank needs the guarantee of Andes Vivos, signed by the director, Inés Cárdenas.

dialogo.texto: La directora está de viaje y vuelve el jueves. ¿Puedo traer el aval firmado ese día?

traduccion.en: The director is away on a trip and comes back on Thursday. Can I bring the signed guarantee that day?

dialogo.texto: Sí, claro. En el supuesto de que usted lo traiga el jueves, el banco puede aprobar el préstamo esa misma semana.

traduccion.en: Yes, of course. In the event that you bring it on Thursday, the bank can approve the loan that same week.

dialogo.texto: Le recomiendo leer la letra pequeña del seguro antes de firmar.

traduccion.en: I recommend that you read the fine print of the insurance before signing.

traduccion.en: I'll read it with Kenji, my coworker. So, in the event that there is a delay of more than thirty days, there is late-payment interest, and if we cancel early, there is no penalty. Is that correct?

dialogo.texto: Exacto. Le preparo los documentos para el jueves.

traduccion.en: Exactly. I'll prepare the documents for you for Thursday.

titulo.en: The future that gives orders

texto.en: In a contract, a law or a set of rules, the simple future does not predict anything: it states an obligation. El arrendatario pagará la renta el día cinco does not mean “he will probably pay”; it means that he must pay. Do not confuse it with the future of probability that you already know (Serán las cinco = it must be five o'clock). A lease speaks in the third person about the two parties: el arrendador (the owner) and el arrendatario (the tenant). It never says tú or yo, and it does not use ir a + infinitive: the simple future is the form of a clause. Read each clause as a rule: El arrendador entregará las llaves el lunes. Las partes podrán prorrogar el contrato.

titulo.en: Deberá, podrá, no podrá + infinitive, and the register

texto.en: Two verbs appear all the time: deber for obligation (deberá + infinitive) and poder for permission (podrá + infinitive). The negative is no podrá, which is a prohibition: El arrendatario no podrá subarrendar la casa. Careful with the order: podrá no subarrendar would mean that he is allowed not to sublet. Put no before podrá. The verb agrees with the subject: el arrendatario deberá, las partes deberán. Compare the spoken and the written register: when you talk you say Tiene que pagar el día cinco, but the clause says El arrendatario deberá pagar el día cinco. The meaning is the same; the written form sounds formal and impersonal.

contexto.en: A February morning in 2031, in the office of a property owner in Mindo. Andes Vivos wants to rent a house to lodge the team during the season. Emma talks to the Propietaria, and they address each other as usted. The Propietaria reads the clauses of the lease, and Emma asks for one more.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, señora García. Bienvenida a Mindo. Aquí tengo el contrato de arrendamiento de la casa.

traduccion.en: Good morning, Ms. García. Welcome to Mindo. Here I have the lease for the house.

dialogo.texto: Muchas gracias. Andes Vivos necesita la casa para alojar al equipo durante la temporada. Quiero revisar bien las cláusulas.

traduccion.en: Thank you very much. Andes Vivos needs the house to lodge the team during the season. I want to review the clauses carefully.

dialogo.texto: Claro que sí. Le voy a leer las cláusulas principales. Primera: el arrendatario pagará una renta de cuatrocientos dólares al mes, el día cinco de cada mes.

traduccion.en: Of course. I'm going to read you the main clauses. First: the tenant will pay a rent of four hundred dollars a month, on the fifth of each month.

dialogo.texto: Cuatrocientos dólares el día cinco. Eso está bien. ¿Qué dice sobre la garantía?

traduccion.en: Four hundred dollars on the fifth. That's fine. What does it say about the deposit?

dialogo.texto: Segunda: el arrendatario entregará una garantía equivalente a un mes de renta, es decir, cuatrocientos dólares.

traduccion.en: Second: the tenant will hand over a deposit equivalent to one month's rent, that is, four hundred dollars.

dialogo.texto: De acuerdo. ¿Hay alguna prohibición?

traduccion.en: Agreed. Is there any prohibition?

dialogo.texto: Tercera: el arrendatario no podrá subarrendar la casa ni tener mascotas.

traduccion.en: Third: the tenant will not be able to sublet the house or keep pets.

dialogo.texto: Eso no es un problema. Vamos a usar la casa solo para el equipo.

traduccion.en: That's not a problem. We are going to use the house only for the team.

dialogo.texto: Cuarta: el arrendatario deberá avisar con treinta días de anticipación si desea terminar el contrato. Es el preaviso.

traduccion.en: Fourth: the tenant must give thirty days' notice if he wishes to end the contract. That is the notice period.

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. En palabras sencillas, tengo que avisar con un mes de anticipación, ¿verdad?

traduccion.en: I understand. In simple words, I have to give a month's notice, right?

dialogo.texto: Exacto. En el contrato se escribe «deberá avisar», pero en una conversación se dice «tiene que avisar». Es lo mismo.

traduccion.en: Exactly. The contract says “deberá avisar”, but in a conversation people say “tiene que avisar”. It is the same thing.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y si queremos prorrogar el contrato?

traduccion.en: And what if we want to extend the contract?

dialogo.texto: Quinta: el contrato terminará al final de la temporada, y las partes podrán prorrogarlo si están de acuerdo. Sexta: el contrato se extinguirá si el arrendatario no paga la renta.

traduccion.en: Fifth: the contract will end at the end of the season, and the parties will be able to extend it if they agree. Sixth: the contract will end if the tenant does not pay the rent.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. ¿La renta incluye el agua y la luz?

traduccion.en: Very good. Does the rent include water and electricity?

dialogo.texto: Sí, el agua y la luz están incluidas. El internet lo paga el arrendatario.

traduccion.en: Yes, water and electricity are included. The tenant pays for the internet.

dialogo.texto: ¿Hay una cláusula penal?

traduccion.en: Is there a penalty clause?

dialogo.texto: Sí. Séptima: si el arrendatario no entrega la casa en la fecha acordada, pagará una penalización por cada día de retraso.

traduccion.en: Yes. Seventh: if the tenant does not hand over the house on the agreed date, he will pay a penalty for each day of delay.

dialogo.texto: Está bien. Pero quiero pedir un cambio: quiero que se añada una cláusula para que el arrendador devuelva la garantía al final.

traduccion.en: That's fine. But I want to ask for a change: I want a clause to be added so that the landlord returns the deposit at the end.

dialogo.texto: Claro. Añado una octava: el arrendador devolverá la garantía al final del contrato, a menos que haya daños en la casa.

traduccion.en: Of course. I'll add an eighth: the landlord will return the deposit at the end of the contract, unless there is damage to the house.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Con esa cláusula estoy de acuerdo.

traduccion.en: Perfect. I agree with that clause.

dialogo.texto: Entonces, ustedes pagan cuatrocientos dólares el día cinco y dejan una garantía de un mes. ¿Es correcto?

traduccion.en: So, you pay four hundred dollars on the fifth and leave a deposit of one month. Is that correct?

dialogo.texto: Es correcto. Hay una cosa más: la directora, la señora Cárdenas, vuelve el jueves y va a firmar el contrato.

traduccion.en: That's correct. There is one more thing: the director, Ms. Cárdenas, comes back on Thursday and is going to sign the contract.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Recuerde que el arrendatario es Andes Vivos. Entonces le preparo una copia para que la revise con su equipo.

traduccion.en: Perfect. Remember that the tenant is Andes Vivos. Then I'll prepare a copy for you to review with your team.

explicacion.en: English can say “Signing the contract, I will give you the keys”, but the Spanish gerund means that the two actions happen at the same time. To say that the signing comes first, use the participle: firmado.
Learners notice the plural but forget the gender. The participle agrees with the noun in gender and in number: las copias → firmadas.

titulo.en: Participle + noun: once something is done

texto.en: The absolute participle puts a past participle in front of a noun to say that one thing is finished before the next one happens: Firmado el contrato, le entrego las llaves. It means “once the contract is signed, I will give you the keys”, and it works like después de firmar el contrato. The participle works like an adjective, so it agrees in gender and number with the noun that follows: firmado el contrato, pagada la garantía, recibidos los documentos, firmadas las copias. English speakers often forget this agreement and say firmado for everything. The structure goes at the beginning of the sentence and a comma separates it from the main clause. It is typical of writing and of formal speech: in an office, at a counter, in a notice.

titulo.en: Which verbs, and what to avoid

texto.en: It works with transitive verbs, the ones that have a direct object that receives the action: firmar el contrato, pagar la garantía, revisar la van, recibir los documentos, entregar las llaves. Some participles are irregular: devolver → devuelto (Devuelta la van, se reembolsará la garantía). The same idea can be said with una vez + participle (Una vez firmado el contrato…) or with después de + infinitive (Después de firmar el contrato…). Do not use the gerund as English does: Firmando el contrato, le entrego las llaves does not mean “once it is signed”. The infinitive alone does not work either: Firmar el contrato, le entrego las llaves is incorrect. The participle must be there, and it must agree.

explicacion.en: English “those who sign” is plural, so learners make the verbs plural too. In a general rule Spanish uses the singular quien with a third person singular verb: quien firme... acepta.
Learners learn that quien takes the subjunctive and use it everywhere. When the person is known, the speaker is stating a fact, so the verb is in the indicative: firmó.
The accent is only for questions and exclamations. In a rule that says “whoever arrives first”, quien has no accent.

titulo.en: Whoever, anyone who: quien + subjunctive

texto.en: Quien + subjunctive means “whoever” or “anyone who”: the person is not known, it can be anybody. Quien firme el contrato acepta las condiciones means that anyone who signs accepts the conditions. It is the language of rules, notices and regulations, and it works like cualquier persona que or la persona que. The verb after quien is in the third person singular, because Spanish treats quien as one person at a time: Quien abra la cuenta deberá presentar la cédula. There is no accent on quien in this use: quién with an accent is only for questions. The main clause often uses the normative future that you already know (deberá, podrá, pagará), and you can combine the rule with a menos que, with en el supuesto de que or with an absolute participle.

titulo.en: A specific person: quien + indicative

texto.en: When the person is known, the verb after quien goes in the indicative: Quien firmó ayer fue Emma. Here the speaker has a concrete person in mind and talks about a fact. Compare: Quien firme (anyone who may sign, subjunctive) and Quien firmó (the person who signed, indicative). The same contrast works with the present: Quien llegue primero elegirá (anybody) and Quien llegó primero fue Kenji (a known person). It is also used in proverbs, which state a general truth: Quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta, which means that if you try to do too much, you do nothing well. Do not use the subjunctive for a known person: Quien firme ayer fue Emma is incorrect. One nuance: in casual speech Spanish also uses the present indicative for a general habit (Quien llega primero, elige), but in rules and notices, and in this course, an unknown person takes the subjunctive.

dialogo.texto: Aquí la tengo. ¿Quién puede retirar dinero?

traduccion.en: Here it is. Who can withdraw money?

dialogo.texto: Quien sea cotitular podrá retirar dinero, a menos que la cuenta esté bloqueada. El retiro se hace en el cajero con la tarjeta.

traduccion.en: Whoever is a joint account holder will be able to withdraw money, unless the account is blocked. The withdrawal is made at the ATM with the card.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y yo podré retirar dinero?

traduccion.en: And will I be able to withdraw money?

dialogo.texto: Sí, porque usted y la directora, la señora Cárdenas, serán las titulares. El beneficiario de los equipos es la comunidad, pero las titulares de la cuenta son ustedes dos.

traduccion.en: Yes, because you and the director, Ms. Cárdenas, will be the account holders. The beneficiary of the equipment is the community, but the account holders are the two of you.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. La directora vuelve el jueves y firmará la solicitud.

traduccion.en: Perfect. The director comes back on Thursday and will sign the application form.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. Firmada la solicitud, el banco entregará una tarjeta en cinco días.

traduccion.en: Very good. Once the application is signed, the bank will deliver a card in five days.

dialogo.texto: ¿Qué pasa con quien no cumpla con un pago?

traduccion.en: What happens to whoever does not meet a payment?

dialogo.texto: Quien incumpla un pago pagará una multa. Es una sanción por el retraso.

traduccion.en: Whoever misses a payment will pay a fine. It is a penalty for the delay.

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. Ayer mi compañero Kenji llamó al banco para preguntar por los retiros. ¿Quién lo atendió?

traduccion.en: I see. Yesterday my coworker Kenji called the bank to ask about withdrawals. Who helped him?

dialogo.texto: Quien lo atendió fue mi colega. Pero quien tenga más dudas sobre los retiros puede preguntarme a mí.

traduccion.en: The person who helped him was my colleague. But whoever has more questions about withdrawals can ask me.

dialogo.texto: ¿Hay algún costo por abrir la cuenta?

traduccion.en: Is there any cost for opening the account?

dialogo.texto: No, abrir la cuenta no tiene costo. Recibida la solicitud firmada, le entregamos un recibo.

traduccion.en: No, opening the account has no cost. Once the signed application is received, we give you a receipt.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y el duplicado de la solicitud?

traduccion.en: And the duplicate of the application?

dialogo.texto: Usted se lleva el duplicado, y el original se queda en el banco.

traduccion.en: You take the duplicate, and the original stays at the bank.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y cuándo llega el desembolso del préstamo para los equipos?

traduccion.en: And when does the disbursement of the loan for the equipment arrive?

dialogo.texto: Firmado el contrato del préstamo, el desembolso se hace dos días después, en esta misma cuenta.

traduccion.en: Once the loan contract is signed, the disbursement is made two days later, into this same account.

dialogo.texto: Gracias. ¿Y si pierdo la tarjeta?

traduccion.en: Thank you. And if I lose the card?

dialogo.texto: En el supuesto de que pierda la tarjeta, llame al banco de inmediato.

traduccion.en: In the event that you lose the card, call the bank immediately.

dialogo.texto: Quiero empezar con una cuenta sencilla. Hay un dicho: quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta.

traduccion.en: I want to start with a simple account. There is a saying: whoever takes on too much does little well.

dialogo.texto: Muy cierto. Empezamos con una cuenta sencilla, y más adelante quien necesite más servicios podrá pedirlos.

traduccion.en: Very true. We start with a simple account, and later whoever needs more services will be able to ask for them.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. ¿Necesita algún otro documento?

traduccion.en: Perfect. Do you need any other document?

dialogo.texto: Solo la cédula de la directora cuando firme. Quien firme la solicitud debe presentar su documento personal.

traduccion.en: Only the director's ID card when she signs. Whoever signs the application must show their personal document.

dialogo.texto: De acuerdo. Muchas gracias por su ayuda. Hasta el jueves.

traduccion.en: Agreed. Thank you very much for your help. See you Thursday.

dialogo.texto: Hasta el jueves, señora García.

traduccion.en: See you Thursday, Ms. García.
